mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS (monthly payrolls) coincides with stronger consumer confidence and higher wage growth, driving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 145,000 and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS as a predictor of SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) followed by a rebound above the prior quarter's level indicates a turning point in supply-side constraints, prompting S&P 500 forward returns to turn positive over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls below prior quarter then crosses above it
failure_condition: No significant mean reversion in SPX 5-day returns following GDPC1 turn-around (AR(1) p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the supply index (INDPRO) remains flat for two consecutive months while inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises, it suggests tight supply conditions that boost risk premium and drive S&P 500 forward returns downward over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prior month and CPIAUCSL > prior month, sustained for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no significant negative correlation with the interaction of INDPRO and CPIAUCSL (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers expectations of tighter policy, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% and remains below for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of UNRATE < 4.5% (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1,200K indicate rebuilding momentum that coincides with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 1200 and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no Granger causality from HOUST (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in monthly retail sales (PAYEMS) followed by a sustained rise above 140K suggests resilient consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS peaks below 135K, then crosses above 140K and sustains for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns show no significant positive relationship with PAYEMS change (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the supply index (INDPRO) remains in contraction for three consecutive months despite falling inflation (CPIAUCSL), it signals persistent supply-side frictions that drive S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prior 3 months and CPIAUCSL < prior 3 months, sustained for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negatively related to the interaction of INDPRO and CPIAUCSL (p > 0.05).
